lineage_specific_terms: Myc Targets V2 (HEI vs HEU, padj 5.3e-07); Myc Targets V2 (HEI vs HEU, padj 5.3e-04); Oxidative Phosphorylation (supp vs unsupp, padj 5.9e-04); G2-M Checkpoint (supp vs unsupp, padj 1.2e-03); Estrogen Response Late (supp vs pre-ART, padj 2.0e-02); Protein Secretion (supp vs pre-ART, padj 2.5e-02); Myc Targets V2 (unsupp vs pre-ART, padj 2.7e-03); G2-M Checkpoint (unsupp vs pre-ART, padj 5.4e-03); E2F Targets (HEU vs HUU, padj 1.7e-04); E2F Targets (HEU vs HUU, padj 4.0e-04)
finding: Proliferation and MYC programmes, not inflammation. Myc targets V2 is significant only in CD4 (Naive 1 and Naive 3, p_adj 5.3e-07) in the infection contrast, E2F targets and DNA repair only in CD4 in the exposure contrast, and G2-M checkpoint and mitotic spindle only in CD4 off treatment. CD4 also carries the largest differential-expression burden of any lineage (23,183 significant gene-by-population calls on treatment versus pre-ART). A cell-cycle readout in infant naive CD4 is a coherent, testable claim and the paper makes none.

lineage_specific_terms: G2-M Checkpoint (HEI vs HEU, padj 2.9e-02); Estrogen Response Early (supp vs pre-ART, padj 4.4e-02)
finding: Almost nothing lineage-specific. Only G2-M checkpoint (p_adj 2.9e-02) and estrogen response early (4.4e-02) are NK-restricted, both borderline, and the viraemia contrast yields 206 significant calls across four populations. NK cells participate in the shared NF-kB and complement programmes but contribute no distinct signal.

lineage_specific_terms: Fatty Acid Metabolism (HEI vs HEU, padj 2.5e-02); Fatty Acid Metabolism (HEI vs HEU, padj 2.6e-02); G2-M Checkpoint (supp vs pre-ART, padj 1.0e-02); G2-M Checkpoint (supp vs pre-ART, padj 4.6e-02); KRAS Signaling Up (unsupp vs pre-ART, padj 3.0e-02); heme Metabolism (HEU vs HUU, padj 1.6e-02); Cholesterol Homeostasis (HEU vs HUU, padj 4.8e-02)
finding: Fatty acid metabolism is B-cell-restricted in the infection contrast across three subsets (transitional, activated and resting naive; p_adj 2.5e-02 to 2.9e-02), with heme metabolism and cholesterol homeostasis appearing in the exposure contrast. Metabolic reprogramming in infant B cells is real but only borderline significant, and the manuscript has no B-cell narrative to attach it to.

lineage_specific_terms: Coagulation (HEI vs HEU, padj 1.7e-04); Xenobiotic Metabolism (HEI vs HEU, padj 1.2e-02); KRAS Signaling Up (supp vs pre-ART, padj 8.7e-03); Coagulation (supp vs pre-ART, padj 1.8e-02); Wnt-beta Catenin Signaling (unsupp vs pre-ART, padj 3.4e-03); Angiogenesis (unsupp vs pre-ART, padj 2.1e-02); Complement (HEU vs HUU, padj 7.3e-07); IL-6/JAK/STAT3 Signaling (HEU vs HUU, padj 1.2e-03)
finding: The only lineage where complement is significant on its own: classical and non-classical monocytes in the HEU-versus-HUU contrast (p_adj 7.3e-07 and 1.3e-03) with IL-6/JAK/STAT3 alongside it (1.2e-03). Coagulation is monocyte-restricted in the infection contrast (1.7e-04). An innate signature that separates exposed-uninfected from unexposed infants bears directly on what HIV exposure alone does, which the paper does not address.

No differential expression was run: the population did not meet the minimum cells-per-group threshold in any contrast, so it is absent from all five output folders. Reported as not assessed rather than as a negative result.

No Hallmark term is unique to gamma-delta T cells in any of the five contrasts. They track the shared programmes with the other lineages. Note separately that the cytotoxic gamma-delta subset is 37% of cells in the CD16+ comparison, which matters for the epitope-database analysis rather than here.

A single population with the smallest differential-expression burden of any lineage (27 significant calls in the viraemia contrast, 173 in the infection contrast) and no unique Hallmark term. Too few cells to support a claim.
